title: Initial founder audit — live public baseline
proof_limits: This is an engineering founder-style walkthrough, not a customer usability study or private-engine audit. UX recommendations are reasoned judgments tied to actual interface observations. Missing future capabilities are not counted as regressions.

findings.task: A: identify the engagement, current stage, blockers and next permitted action
steps: Open the live URL in a fresh browser.
Read the overview and available navigation before loading the sample.
Load the sample and return to the overview.
findings.actual_state: One fictional Acme workspace; overview before and after sample intake.
findings.expected: A compact engagement brief and lifecycle summary should expose the question, deadline, limits, current stage, blocker and next available action.
findings.observed: The overview exposes a claim/comparison, sources and generic navigation. The precise question/deadline/read-only constraints are available only after opening the scope source or report. There is no engagement-stage or review-obligation summary.
findings.implementation_status: Information exists but is distributed and difficult to use as a founder cockpit.
findings.business_impact: Founder must reconstruct context across screens before deciding what to inspect or do next.
findings.smallest_safe_improvement: Add a single fictional engagement brief and state-derived next action, with links to the original scope and existing workflow.

findings.task: A/E: distinguish work not yet performed from insufficient evidence
steps: Open the fresh overview without loading or checking anything.
Compare the prominent comparison card with the adjacent Shadow panel.
findings.actual_state: No sources loaded; internal dataset verdict is NOT RUN.
findings.expected: Every summary should say the comparison has not run until the user runs it.
findings.observed: The comparison card says Not assessed while the adjacent Shadow verification badge says NOT RUN. The missing/stale cases later use NOT ASSESSED as an actual computed result.
findings.implementation_status: Implemented status labels are inconsistent; no false PASS was observed.
findings.business_impact: Founder can confuse an unexecuted check with an evidence-based inability to establish the outcome.
findings.smallest_safe_improvement: Use an explicit Not run state consistently; reserve NOT ASSESSED for a completed comparison with insufficient evidence.

findings.task: F: respond to missing, early or contradictory evidence
steps: Load the sample and run baseline FAIL.
Select observation unavailable and run the check.
Select observation too early and run the check.
Inspect the overview then the internal report.
findings.actual_state: FAIL or NOT ASSESSED displayed with explanatory check details and citations.
findings.expected: The visible blocker should lead to a clear permitted next step, with a distinction between demo actions and real authorized evidence collection.
findings.observed: The dashboard explains the reason but retains the same generic Run fictional check and report navigation. The concrete follow-up is lower in the report; the dashboard does not show an outcome-specific next action or evidence request boundary.
findings.implementation_status: Explanations and follow-up prose exist, but actionable guidance is dispersed.
findings.business_impact: Founder can repeatedly rerun unchanged evidence or mistake a hypothetical variant for resolution of the original discrepancy. Existing what-if labels correctly warn that the baseline is unchanged.
findings.smallest_safe_improvement: Surface a deterministic source-linked next-step explanation for each state; keep real evidence requests unavailable.

findings.task: E/G: understand what a PASS or FAIL does and does not establish
steps: Run hypothetical outcome present.
Read the PASS overview.
Open the report and review provenance, unknowns and release limitations.
findings.actual_state: Hypothetical business outcome PASS; all sample checks pass; native reviews not performed and release not approved.
findings.expected: Business outcome, sample integrity, external authenticity, investigation completeness, Quality, Queen and human release should be visibly separate.
findings.observed: The distinction is truthful in source descriptions, panel captions and report prose, but is not presented as a single ordered set of gates. The dominant PASS is easier to find than the outstanding review/authorization obligations.
findings.implementation_status: Correct proof boundaries exist; founder scanning and review eligibility are difficult.
findings.business_impact: Non-engineers may overread a fictional PASS as a reviewed or releasable engagement despite the detailed disclaimers.
findings.smallest_safe_improvement: Expose separate outcome, evidence, review and release states; show unavailable/not-performed gates without inventing approvals.

findings.task: C/H: understand Queen roles and why the next stage matters
steps: Open Mission timeline, step once, play/pause and reset.
Open Colony map and select every role.
Inspect Queen and Raven responsibilities.
findings.actual_state: Five authored timeline stages and six fixed illustrative roles; no live work.
findings.expected: A founder should connect each illustrated responsibility to its expected input/output and relevant evidence while understanding that nothing is assigned or executing.
findings.observed: Role descriptions and synthetic labels are clear and interactive. The Queen inspector explains coordination generically; no compact mission brief, stage evidence handoff or founder decision appears alongside it.
findings.implementation_status: Existing illustration works; actual assignment/progress/peer-message capability is unavailable by design.
findings.business_impact: Founder can learn the architecture but cannot easily map it to the current fictional engagement lifecycle.
findings.smallest_safe_improvement: Reuse the existing map and authored timeline; add source-linked illustrated responsibilities if useful. No diagram framework replacement is justified by observed behavior.

findings.task: B/C: onboard a real organization and define a real mission
steps: Click the Acme workspace label.
Inspect source-intake scope and available form controls.
Inspect Architecture and Roadmap.
findings.actual_state: One nonselectable fictional workspace and bundled sample intake only.
findings.expected: A future real engagement needs authenticated client identity, written scope, source permissions, question, deadline and constraints.
findings.observed: The label is static and no customer selector, arbitrary upload, authentication or editable mission form exists. The dialog explicitly says no access grant is created. This is a deliberate production boundary, not a broken control.
findings.implementation_status: Not implemented in the public prototype; private implementation not assessed.
findings.business_impact: The public app cannot onboard a customer or authorize a real investigation.
findings.smallest_safe_improvement: Clarify the single fictional engagement and the eventual authenticated interface contract; do not create a public client backend.

findings.task: H: supervise service health, costs, worker reliability and pending business obligations
steps: Inspect overview metrics and every navigation route.
Read Architecture and Roadmap operational capabilities.
findings.actual_state: Source/check counts and zero real model calls; no live service connection.
findings.expected: A real founder console requires attributable workload, cost, reliability, incidents, backups, customer follow-up and pending decisions.
findings.observed: Those operational records and telemetry do not exist in the public interface. The app honestly states no model/customer connection and labels the business capabilities future functionality.
findings.implementation_status: Unavailable here; private/native status intentionally unknown.
findings.business_impact: The public app is not a business operating system or evidence of operational readiness.
findings.smallest_safe_improvement: Show honest connection/availability states; keep numeric telemetry, alerts, costs and customer records absent until canonical authenticated data exists.

findings.task: G/H: obtain review approval, release a report and follow up with a customer
steps: Inspect and export the baseline internal report.
Read the release boundary and all available report controls.
findings.actual_state: Local unapproved fictional Markdown export; no review or delivery record.
findings.expected: A pilot requires full-artifact Quality, Queen acceptance, exact human release, secure delivery and attributable follow-up.
findings.observed: Report export works and is labeled INTERNAL DRAFT / NO RELEASE APPROVAL. No approval, secure customer delivery, billing or follow-up actions exist.
findings.implementation_status: Local export implemented; production review/delivery operations unavailable by design.
findings.business_impact: A file download cannot serve as customer-release authorization or a completed paid engagement.
findings.smallest_safe_improvement: Explain report eligibility and next authorized review step; document future integration rather than adding mock approval controls.

findings.classification: Verified recovery bug under controlled failure
findings.task: B/F: understand and recover from a failed source fingerprint operation
steps: Open sample intake and check consent.
Deliberately reject one SHA-256 operation in this browser only.
Activate Load selected sample.
Restore the original browser hashing implementation.
Inspect error location and retry availability.
Cancel, reopen, consent and retry to confirm successful recovery route.
findings.actual_state: The modal remains open; consent remains checked; no sources were admitted.
findings.expected: A failed intake must expose the actionable error inside the modal and permit a clear retry once the transient failure is gone.
findings.observed: The error is only in the global toast behind the modal backdrop. The load button remains disabled even after hashing is restored; focus stays on the disabled load control. Cancel/reopen/reconsent succeeds, but the recovery is undisclosed.
findings.implementation_status: Recoverable error handling exists but obscures the failure and strands the primary action. The hashing rejection was injected, not a spontaneous platform fault.
findings.business_impact: Founder sees no reason intake stopped and cannot use the visible primary action to recover.
findings.smallest_safe_improvement: Show an accessible inline intake error, restore retry state/focus, and preserve non-admission until all hashes succeed.

findings.task: C: inspect authored timeline stages using the keyboard
steps: Open Mission timeline.
Use Tab until a checkpoint button has focus.
Press Enter.
Repeat for each of the five checkpoint buttons.
findings.actual_state: A checkpoint expands and the timeline DOM is rerendered.
findings.expected: Focus should remain on the activated checkpoint so the keyboard user can continue through the timeline.
findings.observed: All five activations leave document focus on BODY after the focused button is replaced. The next Tab restarts from early page navigation. Role selection retains focus; all source buttons remain keyboard reachable.
findings.implementation_status: Checkpoint selection works, but focus continuity is broken.
findings.business_impact: Keyboard-only founders lose their place and must retraverse page navigation for each stage.
findings.smallest_safe_improvement: Preserve the active data-step identity through timeline rerender, as existing action/role controls already do.

confirmed_working: Bundled fictional intake and source scope
Original source text, SHA-256 display and citation navigation
Baseline FAIL, explicit hypothetical PASS, missing and stale NOT ASSESSED
Insufficient-evidence source fallback and original source download
Internal report export exactly matches displayed Markdown and SHA-256
Illustrative timeline controls and every colony role
Seven routes at desktop/tablet/mobile; zero tablet/mobile overflow
Keyboard skip link, mobile Escape and close/focus behavior
No page errors, unexpected external app requests, backend writes or WebSockets
